Zen, and the art of vintage motorcycle repairs

By: Johann Botha | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
More than a century ago - the first Durban to johannesburg motorcycle race started. Today it is a rally for motorcycles made before 1938 and no longer a race, but still going strong

Summary:
We follow various characters preparing for and eventually taking part in one of the oldest motorcycle events in the world - the DJ rally. Open for pre 1938 bikes, its a prestige event on the motorcycle fanatic's calender and entries come from all over the world. We have some excellent archive footage going back to the first races, which we will intercut with our interviews and with the 2016 rally. Characters we will follow from their preparations in the workshop, to the pre-DJ event and eventually the rally itself, will include the oldest participant, the youngest and also the one with the most DSJ's behind his name. We will also follow the only female participant in the race.

Press Release:


DJ Run
It started as a motorcycle race between Durban and Johannesburg. Over 100 years later it has turned into a rally for vintage motorcycles manufactured as far back as the 1930s. Carte Blanche joins a motley crew of 80 competitors on the DJ Rally, including the female rider of a 1909 classic, eight father and son teams and even two riders over the age of eighty. Who manages the gruelling journey and what fuels their passion for the open road?


Script:



33secs "The early 1900s were a time of beautiful advancement in motorcycle innovation. Models changed dramatically from year to year. Racing was a core element of these developments and in 1913 a Johannesburg to Durban race was launched. People came from far and wide to watch these magnificent men on their low flying machines. With less than 10% of the 650km's tarred, it was a hard ride.
Pierre Cronje spends most of his time with vintage bikes"
Upsound Pierre This is a girder fork here, and its just got this one spring in the centre here, and this moves up and down. And its not very conducive for bad roads.
13secs "The early bikes had no clutch or gearbox, and had to be push-started. And, one had to pump fresh oil into the engine all the time as it simply burnt out on the ride.
Trevor Jones is another collector who knows these machines inside out"
Upsound As this plunger works its way up again – I can normally go about 8km's and then I push it down again and it starts the whole sequence again.
44secs " In 1935 Roy Hasketh set the fastest ever time for the race on an Excelsior – 6 hours, 41 minutes and 51 seconds. The longest finishing time went to Fred Zurcher on his Douglas, who won it in 23 hours, 18minutes and 20 seconds thanks to heavy snow on the Drakensberg.
The race came to an end in 1936 when racing on public roads was banned.
But the machines and the passion remained. And, in 1971 it was revived – not as a race, but as a timed rally.
Pierre says that only verified pre-1936 bikes can be entered. "
Pierre in workshop The only one eligible here for the DJ is this little Douglas, very interesting bike
MAP The DJ is now mostly run in the opposite direction, from Durban to Johannesburg.
Pierre is confident that his baby is ready for this year’s event
Pierre talks us thorugh his bike This is a nice one it goes well.... a lot of power
17secs The oldest competitor to complete the race yet, was 90 year old Stuart Cunningham back in 2013. This year the oldest rider is Neville Smith who is 81. He has already done the DJ 26 times.
Neville "I get a lot of pleasure out of these old bikes, you know. I've been working on them since I was a 14 year old kid, so it's in my blood you know. It's like the common cold, there is no cure it just carries on and on
Derek: You just have to fix the oil leaks
Ive also got a few oil leaks..laughs..."
11secs Sam Anderson is one of only two female riders this year. She rides in front, because she's on the oldest bike. We caught up with her in the basement, in the early morning dark, half an hour before the start.
Sam "Derek: Surely its got a name?
Sam: Cantankerous old bastard."
Derek opening link It's a bright and early 6am start for the start, and there's good reason for that – they want to get to newcastle before Sunset

10secs Sam's 1909 Humber is basically a glorified bicycle and she needs to pedal when the motor struggles uphill. But that is only one of the challenges.
10secs The route map tells you where to drive and how fast to go. How you work it out is another story as stopwatches are the only gauges allowed on the bike
Pierre There are 84 white lines to a km. If you do 60...
18secs Every second over or under the specified time for each stage equals one penalty point, and the rider with the least amount of penalty points is the overall winner. Riders start one minute apart. Pierre is on number 15, with Neville right in front of him on number 14.
MAP AND ROAD SIGNS Stage 1 follows the Comrades route from Hillcrest to Pietermaritzburg for the first fuel stop.
Neville The bike is going well... the rally is concerned
MAP AND ROAD SIGNS AND ONE OR TWO SCENIC SHOTS WITH MUSIC The riders now have to go through the hilly KZN midlands to Estcourt where lunch awaits.
7secs The riders are gradually beginning to feel the effects of the bumps and potholes, and, by now, a few bikes are also giving problems.
Upsound orange helmet No 25
4secs Fortunately Sam's number 1 is still going strong
Up sounds Sam
10secs As current clerk of the course, Ian Holmes and his team did most of the work, laying out and timing the course, and overseeing the whole event.
Interview ian holmes Th bikes are props to a great people event
Ladysmith sign From Estcourt to Ladysmith where, just before reaching town, we find Pierre beside the road
Sequence Pierre and Derek
MAP AND THEN ARCHIVE AND THEN ROAD SIGN NEWCASTLE And then on to Newcastle, for the overnight stop. Since the first race 103 years ago, Newcastle has always welcomed participating riders.
Soundup Sam Very happy to be here, but im very tired
14secs "Day 1 is usually the day when most bikes give trouble. Though ten bikes broke down on day 1, it seems there may be fewer casualties than in past years.

Riders tell us that once you've done your first DJ you keep coming back. And you pass it on to the next generation. On this year's entry list - 8 pairs of family members are riding together."
MAP DAY 2. START LADISMITH ENDS GERMISTON Day 2, and the 72 remaining riders have to go from newcastle through Volksrust, Standerton, Balfour and Heidelberg to the end point in Germiston.

Derek link For the bodies and bikes that have survived, its another testing day ahead. With a lot of pressure on the overnight leader Gavin Walton, on his 1936 AJS
4secs Gavin only had 55 penalty points against him after day 1
Gavin Im pretty happy with my score, its like golf – the lower the better.
9secs As Gavin gets going we get word that Sam is out of the race. We catch up with her just outside town where the paramedics are treating her burnt leg.
Sam Petrol fell out of the bike...and rolled in the grass.


"MAP
SCENIC SHOTS
BIKES RIDING
MUSIC" The windy road through the Drakensberg results in a few more casualties
Archive of bikes struggling as it has done since the first race 103 years ago...
5secs As we come round a bend, we see that Pierre's race is also over...
Pierre Ek dink syt genoeg geh
"MAP
HEIDELBERG SIGN
MUSIC" Lunch awaits in Heidelberg, a mere 50 odd km's from the finish line.
3secs Neville, arrives in good spirits for an octogenarian...
Interv Neville
"MAP
" The rally ends at the clubhouse of the CMC in Germiston. In total, 20 bikes broke down. It was more than expected and begs the question - how many years do these charismatic steel horses have left in them before metal fatigue finally claims them?
Derek link But for the top riders it’s too soon to celebrate. They'll only know if they've won the trophy at the breakfast tomorrow morning.
9secs Sunday morning's prize giving breakfast in Sandton sees two tables full of silver ware. But, the big prize is the original Schlesinger Trophy
Announcing winner
32secs "Ralph only had 230 penalty points, meaning that over 641 km's he was off the timing specs by less than 4 minutes. And Gavin, the overnight leader came in second, 25 points behind Ralph.
In the end all 62 riders who finished feel they are winners. With a proud history stretching back over a century, the DJ is about far more than first prize. It’s about the journey, the camaraderie, the fun and the pain, and about coming back to ride again next year."
